correctness.rationale: Let d=2^k u, u odd. Mismatches at n=2^k q-1 with q=2 mod4 occur every 4*2^k, ruling out u>=5 because comparisons need length>=d; for u=3 additional q=3 mod4 mismatches rule out that case. For dyadic d=2^k, q=1 or 2 mod4 are forced mismatches with gaps<=3d and at n=d-1,2d-1, giving start a>=2d and factor length<=4d-1, so endpoint a+length<3a. Dyadic blocks p[2^j:2^(j+1)) are squares of period 2^(j-1), giving r-factor construction. Any factorization from initial index 2 to final 2^(r+1) has s>r log_3 2 hence s>=floor(r log_3 2)+1. Finite independent DP for r<=8 and exhaustive bounded mismatch checks match proof.
residual_risks: No exact width claimed for each r; all-size conclusions rely on 2-adic modular mismatch proof, not finite scan.

value.rationale: A natural shortest-factorization invariant in a canonical uniformly recurrent automatic word exhibits explicit logarithmically growing lower bounds despite bounded monochromatic runs, demonstrating genuine periodic structure rather than trivial long constant blocks.
residual_risks: No exact optimal sw(W_r) formula or decidability for arbitrary automatic words is shown.

final_claim: For the classical period-doubling word p(n)=nu_2(n+1) mod 2, witness factors W_r=p[2:2^(r+1)) have floor(r log_3 2)+1 <= minimal repetition-factorization width <=r for all r>=1, hence unbounded shortest width; all genuine repetition periods are powers of two.
limitations: No general automatic-word decidability or exact all-factor widths
